key_insight: The paper turns nonlinear aggregation-diffusion PDEs into a variational neural transport problem, learning a velocity field that moves particle densities while respecting the continuity equation.
engineering_relevance: This offers a mesh-free, optimization-based solver for transport-driven PDEs that can be useful in chemotaxis, polymer dynamics, and other large-scale continuum models.
method: Use the Onsager variational principle to recast the PDE as a constrained optimal control problem.
Parameterize the transport velocity with a neural network and train it using a variational loss evaluated along particle trajectories.
Couple density and generalized score evolution with an Euler-time stepping scheme to efficiently propagate the score for loss computation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments on several representative models, and the paper also provides a rigorous error analysis separating approximation, optimization, Monte Carlo sampling, and time-discretization errors.
watch_item: Performance depends on stable training and accurate score propagation, so discretization and sampling choices may strongly affect results.
paper_title: Variational neural transport for aggregation-diffusion equations
